rv.q: Call "Tina" a jukebox musical or a bio-musical or anything you want to call it, but above all, this is one fine specimen in the best showbiz tradition of the Great Big Broadway Musical.
The show’s flaws fade away next to the star’s incandescence.
And Adrienne Warren, who nails each impossible note up in that fifth octave and way down in the gravel, every swivel and swagger, and each last defiant, self-actualizing rasp, is simply the best.
The show finds its groove when Ms. Warren is allowed to inhabit the role fully, channeling Turner's fierce energy and distinctive vocal style with impressive conviction.
Warren’s galvanizing turn is, in every sense, in the same league as those Tony winners.
Hers isn’t so much a performance as an eruption.
Unfortunately even a transcendent performance cannot lift a mediocre musical to stratospheric heights — or at least it can do so only intermittently.
If you meant to see a true union of song and story, though, you won’t get it here.
Warren delivers a performance of superhuman stamina and skill.
But Tina, as spectacularly played by Broadway’s better-be-good for a Tony nomination star Adrienne Warren, is the show.
But fortunately, with Adrienne Warren in the title role, this one has at least one element that lets it stand better than almost all the rest.

Though Warren shines consistently, the vehicle for her bright performance, Tina: The Tina Turner Musical, hits several road bumps while charting the icon's life from childhood through her Eighties comeback.
Pretty much every note of nuance is lost in the razzle-dazzle rush.
The repetition of the play's mechanics turns all Cyrano’s wit and briskness into an inner torment that goes nowhere.
But like them, Hall’s book covers too much biographical ground too quickly.
The ensemble does little besides adding back-up singing and functions like window dressing.
Tina, for all its huffing and puffing, doesn't capture the force of nature she was in live performance.
She does so with heartbreaking passion, but the other pieces of this colorful, moving mosaic are just as vivid.

It's not at all a lousy show, but Adrienne Warren's performance in the title role has the roaring lift of a helicopter taking flight and the dazzling sparkle of a hundred chandeliers, making Tina a musical not to miss.
This alone is worth the ticket.
Warren is absolutely stunning in the titular role.
